title: Dedicated capacity: customer journey mapping for SLA tiers, reserved throughput, and automated fallback strategy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Define a customer-facing intake and prioritization artifact that maps the full customer journey for Dedicated (reserved) capacity requests into concrete SLA tier definitions, recommended reserved throughput profiles, GPU family guidance, and an automated fallback policy for capacity shortages. The artifact will be used by Solutions, Sales, and Customer Success during intake and by Product/Eng to scope Dedicated onboarding and capacity planning. Scope: - Produce an intake matrix that translates customer requirements (latency SLO, p50/p95, concurrency, throughput QPS, burst patterns, acceptable degradation behavior) into one of three SLA tiers. - For each SLA tier, prescribe default reserved throughput profiles (tokens/s and QPS), recommended GPU families and sample fleet sizes, and typical cost delta estimates. - Define conditional autoscaling and burst policies (min/max, preemptible burst behavior) and mandatory fallback behavior (model variant fallback, region reroute, degraded feature sets) for when reserved capacity is exceeded. - Include a short decision guide for when to escalate to Enterprise Solutions (security/compliance, air-gapped, custom kernel tuning). Out of scope: per-customer custom pricing negotiation and detailed infra placement decisions that require billing/legal review.
acceptance_criteria: Intake matrix with at least three SLA tiers (Standard / Premium / Critical) and example customer signals mapped to each tier.

For each SLA tier: a recommended reserved throughput profile (tokens/sec and estimated concurrent requests), default GPU family recommendation, and sample fleet size example for a 100M monthly token workload.
Fallback strategy documented with ordered actions (region failover, model variant downgrade, rate-limiting) and expected user-visible consequences.
Operational runbook stub for Solutions/Success to follow during onboarding with required artifacts (network diagram, KMS decision, compliance checkbox).
Stakeholder review and sign-off from Sales, Solutions, Eng Infra, and Legal recorded in comments/links.
proposed_sla_tiers: Standard: p50 < 150ms, p95 < 600ms, best-effort burst to 2x reserved throughput, customer impact low
Premium: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 250ms, guaranteed burst window up to 3x reserved throughput for 5 minutes, customer impact medium
Critical: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 120ms, reserved throughput with hot-standby lanes and automatic regional failover, customer impact high
recommended_gpu_families: Standard: NVIDIA A10 / T4 equivalent (cost-optimized, supports quantized 8-bit variants)
Premium: NVIDIA A100 40GB or equivalent (balanced FP16 and int8 performance)
Critical: H100 or latest high-throughput family with NVLink where available (low-latency, large KV cache)
throughput_profiles: Light: 10k tokens/day ~ 5 tokens/sec reserved, 1 concurrent request typical
Medium: 1M tokens/day ~ 200 tokens/sec reserved, 10 concurrent requests typical
High: 100M tokens/day ~ 20k tokens/sec reserved, 200 concurrent requests typical
scaling_policies: Autoscale conservative: min=1x reserved, max=2x reserved; scale up if sustained >80% utilization for 60s; scale down if <30% for 120s
Autoscale aggressive: min=1x reserved, max=4x reserved; scale up if >60% for 30s (used for Premium only)
Burst policy: short-lived preemptible nodes for 5-10 minute windows; customers can opt-in with costs explained

Fallback order: 1) model-variant downgrade (smaller model or quantized), 2) regional failover to secondary region, 3) feature degrade (disable non-critical multimodal ops), 4) soft rate-limit with user-visible guidance
